# Mathematical notes on cote 79, scans 175–189

## What the pages do

**M1 · Scans 175–176, (56)–(57).** A commuting triangle links $Z$, $G$ and $Z'$. The numbered data include a quotient $G_0$ of the triangular cartographic group, a subgroup generated by two of the $\tau$'s, subgroups $\widetilde B''$ and $B'$, and maps between two extensions. The diagram in d) relates the induced quotient map to squaring on $Z$. The closing paragraph asks when these data come from a graph with homotheties.

**M2 · Scans 177–178, (58)–(62).** A largely cancelled draft tests adjacency of $\{s,t\}$ against adjacency of $\{f^{-1}s,f^{-1}\lambda t\}$. Scan 178 makes the dependence on the class of $f$ explicit, expresses both endpoints using a base point, and introduces a representative $\rho$ taking $s_0$ to $t_0$. Existence of $w,w'$ gives the two tests in (62). The announced next formula is absent before the new chapter.

**M3 · Scan 179, (1)–(3).** Chapter X defines two points of a homogeneous $G$-set to be $G$-equivalent when their stabilizers coincide. Evaluation at $s_0$ identifies its class with an orbit of the commutant $Z$. The page compares that orbit with the points fixed by $G_{s_0}$.

**M4 · Scans 180–181, (4)–(14).** Choosing an origin identifies $S$ with $G/U$. The normalizer quotient describes the equivariant bijections. For all equivariant self-maps, (11) uses evaluation at the origin and (13) gives a right translation. The author explicitly draws attention to the inverse on $a$ in (7) and the order of factors in (14).

**M5 · Scans 182–183, (15)–(16).** The text lists three circumstances in which the orbit and the fixed-point set coincide: a finite set, finite stabilizers, or the stated real Lie group hypotheses on the stabilizers. Antipodal points and strictly antipodal points are distinguished through the corresponding maps and their images. The strict relation is identified with the original equivalence relation.

**M6 · Scans 183–185, (17)–(19).** The homogeneous set becomes the vertices of a connected regular combinatorial 2-polyhedron. A note restricts the discussion to triangular faces. For an element commuting with $G_0$, condition (17) moves the two ends of an edge by mutually inverse operations. Formula (18) describes the resulting movement of a star. Transitivity on oriented edges reduces the test to one fixed edge.

**M7 · Scans 185–186, (20)–(24′).** An element $a$ in a normalizer represents the action of $\lambda$ on $s_0$. The calculation uses the stabilizers of the two ends of the reference edge and arrives at $\rho(a)a\in\widetilde U_1\widetilde U_0$. The figure locates three reflection labels relative to that edge. The oriented version uses $G_0^+$ and untilded subgroups.

**M8 · Scans 186–187, the second (25) through (27).** The author forms a graph with twisted edge set $A_\lambda$. Strictness is expressed by a graph isomorphism. Formula (26) identifies the original star at $s$ with the twisted star at $\lambda s$. The rotation groups around those vertices lead to a parameter for the change of polygon structure, taken modulo sign.

**M9 · Scan 188, (28)–(30).** Transport by $G_0$ makes the parameter independent of the chosen vertex. The twisted edges are recovered by taking the union of the edge sets on the stars. The text proposes local hypotheses for this reconstruction: each star carries a combinatorial polygon and each twisted edge lies in a star. Because the group acts transitively, the tests are reduced to one star and one edge.

**M10 · Scan 189, (31)–(32).** Existence of a triangle leads to an intersection of two original stars. A path of three edges connects $s$ to $\lambda^{-1}s$. The page discusses distance three, the identity at distance zero, and the antipodal octahedron at distance two.

**Reading question T1, scan 186 L15–20.** In the comparison just below the second (25), the frozen reading of the subscript on $A$ is `0`, with `\lambda` as its alternative. The low loop supports zero, but the rising stroke also permits lambda. This affects the identity of the graph in the strictness test described in M8.

## Remarks of the model

- **R1 · My observation, high confidence, scan 179.** Freeness of the commutant action follows from transitivity: a commuting permutation fixing $s_0$ fixes every $gs_0$. This checks the freeness clause of P1.
- **R2 · My observation, high confidence, scans 180–181.** Evaluating two right translations $gU\mapsto gaU$ in succession gives $gabU$. This checks the order of the subscripts in (14) independently of the overwritten letter naming the maps. A typographic identification of that letter with an earlier $f$ would have low confidence.
- **R3 · My observation, high confidence, scan 184.** The symmetry of unordered pairs recovers the converse of (17′): apply the forward implication to the twisted edge with its two ends interchanged. The two inverse actions then cancel.
- **R4 · My observation, high confidence, scan 189.** A point in the intersection in (31) supplies the middle vertex after $t$ in the drawn path. This checks the implication from that intersection to the distance bound in (32).
- **R5 · My observation, high confidence for the example, scan 189.** In the six-vertex octahedral graph, each vertex and its opposite have the same four neighbours and are at distance two. A finite adjacency calculation checked all six vertices. This check concerns the octahedron example. Classification of all the possible distance-two cases in P6 remains open in this reading.
